scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Jathilan originated in Ponorogo, East Java, Indonesia.

Hypotheses regarding its broader development suggest it may have emerged as a ritual reenactment of battle during Prince Diponegoro's war against Dutch colonial forces, or earlier based on Mataram-era troops riding against the Dutch.
In East Java, it developed as an integral part of the Reog Ponorogo performance.
on_screen: Map: Indonesia · Southeast Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Jathilan and related horse dances are performed to celebrate special life events, such as boys' circumcisions or rites of passage, as well as for public entertainment.
The dance portrays troops riding horses and military virility.
In modern community settings such as Yogyakarta, Jathilan art associations like Turonggo Wiro Budoyo serve as active social gathering spaces for local youth.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Performers dance while straddling flat hobbyhorses made from woven bamboo or rattan.
Groups traditionally consist of two to eight dancers who move across a cordoned-off performance space separated from the audience.
Dancers portray troops riding horses, executing choreographed riding movements.
Watch for Hobbyhorse riding.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Performances are accompanied by traditional musical instruments, including the angklung, gongs, and dog-dog drums.
In related regional forms like Balinese Sang Hyang Jaran, the audience may also participate by forming a chorus and singing.
Listen for the angklung, gongs, dog-dog drums.

A driving percussive acoustic texture driven by interlocking angklung, deep gongs, and the rhythmic beat of dog-dog drums, punctuated by the metallic jingle of small bells strung around the dancers' ankles.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Turonggo Wiro Budoyo (TWB) is an active jathilan art association based in the Wirobrajan district of Yogyakarta.
The dance is known as Kuda Lumping in West Java, Jaran Kepang in Central Java, Jathilan in East Java, and Sang Hyang Jaran in Bali.
Jathilan belongs to the broader Javanese hobbyhorse dance tradition and is specifically embedded within the Reog Ponorogo performance tradition of East Java.

Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Jathilan is variant of Kuda Lumping: West Javanese variant of the flat hobbyhorse dance, often featuring trance and magic displays.
Jathilan is variant of Jaran Kepang: Central Javanese variant of the woven hobbyhorse dance tradition.
Jathilan is parent of Reog Ponorogo: East Javanese performance complex of which Jathilan is a core component.
Jathilan is sibling of Sang Hyang Jaran: Balinese hobbyhorse trance dance accompanied by chorus singing.
